item.title: Boston Celtics vs. Chicago Bulls: Stream, lineups, injury reports, broadcast (10/26)
item.description: The Boston Celtics will play host to the Chicago Bulls at their own home arena of TD Garden to face the Central Division for the first of two meetings this week. The Celtics are going to be looking to keep their record in the win column after having done as much vs. the reigning NBA champion New York Knicks on Friday (Oct. 23) night, also at TD Garden. The Bulls, for their part, will be looking to get back to winning games again after having lost their last tilt to the new-look Washington Wizards . We expect a Celtics win in this contest, but this is a better iteration of Chicago than Boston has faced in recent seasons, if not especially so. Records, standing, and streaks At present, the Celtics have a 1-1 record in the midst of the early-season Eastern Conference scrum. The Bulls are the owners of a 1-2 record heading into this contest, further down the crowded East standings. Player injuries For Boston, only Devin Carter (illness) is out. For Chicago, Nic Claxton (hamstring) is out, and Noa Essengue (head contusion) and Patrick Williams (groin) are questionable. item.title: Klint Kubiak issues intriguing message about Raiders’ outlook after loss to Rams
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Klint Kubiak issues intriguing message about Raiders’ outlook after loss to Rams appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a hot start, the Las Vegas Raiders have now lost four straight games. The Raiders fell to the Los Angeles Rams , 35-21, at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday, dropping to 3-4, including 1-3 at home. Las Vegas tried to rally in the fourth quarter, but the Rams proved to be too much, with Matthew Stafford carving up the defense. The Raiders have given up an average of 35.7 points in their losing streak. Los Angeles carried a 22-point lead at halftime, 28-6. Still, coach Klint Kubiak said he did not consider replacing Kirk Cousins with Fernando Mendoza in the second half, stating that they made it a “very competitive game” in the third quarter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kubiak, however, admitted that they have a lot of soul-searching to do. “I think we have to go watch the film, and I think at this point, we’re thinking about everything. How to fix our problems. How to fix our issues in the red zone. Third quarter, personnel, scheme. We have to talk about everything,” said Kubiak in the video posted by the Las Vegas Review-Journal’s Sam Gordon. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said he did not consider turning in the second half to Fernando Mendoza at quarterback. When asked about when he starts thinking about the future of the franchise, Kubiak said “I think at this point, we’re thinking about everything.” More: pic.twitter.com/YwdOdeq42r — Sam Gordon (@BySamGordon) October 25, 2026 Cousins threw 26-of-44 for 295 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Mendoza, the No. 1 draft pick in April, has only appeared in one game, going 6-of-8 for 48 yards in garbage time against the New England Patriots in Week 5. Las Vegas has now dropped four straight games to Los Angeles. “No one’s coming to help us. We’ve got to figure it out ourselves as a coaching staff, with the players, and we have to complement each other as well because we’ve got to start the game a lot faster offensively,” said Kubiak in a report from the Associated Press’ Mark Anderson. The Raiders will visit the New York Jets in Week 8. item.title: Lions Walk Off Packers With Last Second Field Goal
item.description: Photo by: Junfu Han Detroit Edges Green Bay in Dramatic NFC North Showdown The Detroit Lions earned a dramatic 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday at Ford Field, as kicker Jake Bates drilled a 22 yard field goal as time expired to give Detroit a crucial divisional win. The Lions improved to 4-2 with their second consecutive victory, while the Packers fell to 4-3 and saw their three-game winning streak come to an end. Both teams had opportunities to take control, but costly mistakes and missed chances kept the game close until the final seconds. Jared Goff Connects With Jameson Williams Detroit’s offense found success through the air, with quarterback Jared Goff delivering another strong performance. Goff completed 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns without throwing an interception. Both touchdown passes went to wide receiver Jameson Williams, who finished with five receptions for 91 yards. Williams opened the scoring with a 16 yard touchdown catch in the first quarter before adding a 10-yard score in the third. Amon-Ra St. Brown also played a major role in Detroit’s victory. He caught nine passes for 153 yards, consistently creating problems for Green Bay’s secondary. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs contributed 116 rushing yards on 29 carries while adding five receptions for 27 yards. However, a costly fumble prevented Detroit from extending its lead before halftime. Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love completed 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. Packers Miss Costly Opportunities The Packers answered Detroit’s opening touchdown with a scoring connection between Love and tight end Tucker Kraft. Green Bay later took the lead when Love found running back Josh Jacobs for a 25-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Jacobs, making his season debut, finished with 36 rushing yards and 55 receiving yards, including the touchdown catch. Detroit responded with Williams’ second touchdown to take a 17-14 lead. Green Bay eventually tied the game at 17-17 with a 43 yard field goal from rookie kicker Trey Smack. The Packers had an opportunity to take the lead late in the fourth quarter, but Smack missed a 35-yard field goal attempt that was blocked by Detroit defensive end D.J. Wonnum. The block proved to be the turning point. Detroit took possession and put together a 71 yard drive, with Goff making several important throws to move the offense into scoring position. Bates Delivers the Game Winner Detroit managed the clock during the final possession, setting up Bates for the decisive 22 yard field goal with one second remaining. The victory gives the Lions an important early advantage in the NFC North race. Detroit’s offense showed its explosive potential, while the defense and special teams delivered when the game was on the line. For Green Bay, the missed field goals and inability to capitalize on key opportunities proved costly. The Packers will look to regroup quickly, with another divisional matchup again

item.description: Without leading scorer Paolo Banchero, the Orlando Magic overcame a choppy start on Sunday to defeat the New York Knicks , marking their first win under coach Sean Sweeney. Franz Wagner narrowly missed a triple-double with 23 points, a career-high 13 points and nine assists, while Desmond Bane scored 22 points and Tristan da Silva added 19 points off the bench in the 111-102 victory at Madison Square Garden. The Magic trailed 12-0 early after missing their first eight shots of the game. They rallied back to within one possession on several occasions, and they wouldn't take their first lead until the 7:25 mark of the fourth quarter on a free throw by Wagner. Orlando outscored New York 40-27 in the fourth quarter, including a 35-16 run to finish. The group made several defensive stops in key situations and forced seven of the Knicks' 16 total turnovers in the period, which resulted in 10 points. While Banchero missed his first game after suffering a low-grade high right ankle sprain on Friday, the Magic saw Anthony Black return from his own injury. Black provided an immediate spark, finishing with 18 points, five assists and three rebounds in 26 minutes. item.title: Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase reveals heated wake-up call that sparked comeback vs. Ravens
item.description: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase reveals heated wake-up call that sparked comeback vs. Ravens appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ja’Marr Chase was not happy with the first-half display the Cincinnati Bengals put out on the field against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday afternoon. It resulted in the star receiver expressing a loud and clear message to everyone in the locker room. Going into the game, Cincinnati had a 3-2 record. Chase and the squad yearn to get back to the playoffs after last appearing in 2022. Boasting health on offense, their ceiling looks better than it has been in past seasons. They had a slow start against their division rival, being scoreless at halftime. Despite this, they stormed back as they torched Baltimore for the rest of the game. Chase reflected on the offense’s return to form after the game, revealing what he said to his teammates in the locker room during the halftime break. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I came in here screaming: somebody’s got to make a play for us,” Chase said, per reporter Jeremy Rauch. "I came in here screaming: somebody's got to make a play for us." Strong reaction from Ja'Marr Chase on his halftime message to the team (via @GSorrentinoTV ). #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/4acLRz3P11 — Jeremy Rauch (@FOX19Jeremy) October 25, 2026 How Ja’Marr Chase, Bengals played against Ravens Ja’Marr Chase and the Bengals are making noise in a competitive AFC North Division. Their blowout win over the Ravens will be beneficial to their position in the playoff picture later down the road. Baltimore had the initial upper hand over Cincinnati, leading 13-0 at halftime. The Bengals fired back with sheer offensive dominance, torching the Ravens by scoring the last 35 points of the day. Joe Burrow was relentless with his passing, allowing his star receivers to flourish. He completed 22 out of 30 passes for 292 yards and four touchdowns. Chase Brown led the run game with 11 carries for 39 yards, while Samaje Perine rushed four times for 16 yards and a touchdown. Tee Higgins led receivers with six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown. Chase came next with five receptions for 62 yards and a touchdown, while Drew Sample and Mike Gesicki caught touchdown passes. The Bengals will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Tennessee Titans in Week 8 as kickoff commences on Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET. item.title: Kirk Cousins sends clear ‘don’t want to be out’ message to Raiders as major QB pressure builds
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images Kirk Cousins has made his stance clear on the possibility of losing his starting job with the Las Vegas Raiders, insisting he does not want to be on the field if he is no longer the team’s best option. The veteran quarterback’s comments come as pressure builds on head coach Klint Kubiak to consider rookie Fernando Mendoza following the Raiders’ fourth consecutive defeat. Las Vegas fell to a 3-4 record after losing 35-21 to the Los Angeles Rams, raising fresh questions about whether Cousins should continue leading the offence. Kirk Cousins backs Fernando Mendoza as Las Vegas Raiders consider quarterback change Cousins threw two touchdown passes against the Rams, taking his season total to 16, but his lack of mobility has become a concern as the Raiders struggle to find consistency. Speaking about the possibility of being replaced by Mendoza, Cousins made it clear that winning must come before his own position. “If I’m not the best option, then I don’t want to be out there either,” Cousins said. “I want our football team to have the best chance to win games.” The 38-year-old also praised Mendoza, acknowledging the rookie’s progress while making it clear that he intends to keep performing at his best. Cousins added: “The organization will do what they feel is best, but I feel that Fernando’s done a great job and has a bright future ahead.” Despite the growing debate over his future, Cousins has continued to produce touchdowns. His 16 passing scores tie the Raiders’ franchise record for the most by a quarterback through his first seven games with the team, matching Daryle Lamonica and Jeff George. Only Lamonica, who threw 20 touchdowns in his first seven games of the 1969 season, has managed more for the franchise across that span. However, Kubiak has not ruled out a change under centre. Asked whether Mendoza could start against the New York Jets, the Raiders head coach said: “We’re thinking about everything.” That leaves Cousins facing mounting pressure ahead of the next game, with the Raiders desperate to end their losing run. If Las Vegas decides to turn to Mendoza, Cousins could also become a trade candidate, with the New York Giants, Minnesota Vikings and Cleveland Browns mentioned as potential destinations, according to the rumours. For now, the decision rests with Kubiak, who must weigh Cousins’ touchdown production against the need to get the struggling Raiders back on track. item.title: NC State parts ways with defensive coordinator DJ Elliot, football general manager
item.description: A day after the firing of head football coach Dave Doeren , NC State announced that defensive coordinator DJ Eliot has been relieved of his duties. On Sunday, the university said that Charlton Warren will handle the defensive play calling for the remainder of the season. Zac Roper will coach the running backs and coordinate special teams. The staff shakeups come after a road loss Friday night at Stanford , 31-28, that dropped the Wolfpack to 1-3 in the ACC and 3-4 overall. On Saturday, a source close to the program and a university spokesperson told ABC11 that football general manager Andy Vaughn had also been fired. Defensive coordinator DJ Elliot was let go a day after head coach Dave Doeren was fired. Behind the head coach, the general manager is the person most responsible for building a roster. Interim head coach Todd Goebbel will hold his first media briefing on Tuesday, NC State said. Fans who spoke to ABC11 on Sunday said this was tough to see, especially in the middle of a season, but they also said they saw these changes as inevitable. Many expected Doeren would be out after this season, but what few expected was a mid-season shakeup. "Absolutely. You know, I was kind of surprised to see that yesterday. I thought that he was kind of going to get, you know, let go at the end of the season," said Luke Wallace, an NC State junior. "And I didn't think it was going to be right in the middle of the season. You know, I have a couple of friends on the football team, and they were kind of surprised as well." NC State alum Will Hutchens is firmly convinced as to who should be the next hire. "Yeah. And I think you go all in on Philip Rivers, whether that's as the head coach, if he wants a head coaching job, you give it to him. If you get him in here as maybe a general manager-type role and let him bring in his guys, I think the money will flow in if Rivers is a part of the program and that matters today." One NC State fan was delighted by the unexpected developments. "Last night I saw it on the news, and it made my day because I knew it was coming," Robby Crawford said. Talk of Rivers, the NC State quarterbacking legend as the possible next head coach, was prominent across campus. It'd be cool if Phil Rivers becomes our coach," Crawford said. "Give it a shot. Let's make it fun again." Another NC State fan, Cassidy Harmer, agreed. "I hope he comes back. I love him; he was a great player. All his highlights are absolutely insane," she said. "And it's what the team needs: A fresh face, someone who knows our team, what it's like to play at Carter-Finley." - ABC11's Kate Rogerson and Tom George contributed.

item.title: Rocco Baldelli withdraws from Mariners manager search
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 2: Manager Rocco Baldelli #5 of the Minnesota Twins looks on against the Chicago White Sox in the eighth inning of the game at Target Field on September 2, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the biggest names remaining in the Mariners’ managerial search has reportedly withdrawn from contention, reports Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic: Rocco Baldelli has reportedly taken himself out of the running, citing “family considerations.” Baldelli, 45, is originally from Rhode Island, and spends part of his time there, but also has a home in St. Petersburg, Florida, where he was based during his seven-year professional playing career as a member of the Rays. For the past year, he’s been working with the Dodgers as a special assistant/advisor to president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman. Perhaps that was enough being cross-coastal for Baldelli, who has three children under age five, including three-year-old twins. Baldelli has been a popular name in the Mariners’ coaching search thanks to a strong reputation for facility with analytics. He joined the Rays front office shortly after his playing career ended and was with the organization – arguably the most analytics-friendly front office in the sport – until he departed to take the Twins’ managerial vacancy. Baldelli was with Minnesota from 2019-2025, overseeing the Twins in three playoff appearances but also a deeply disappointing 2024 where the team finished fourth in the AL Central despite being favored in preseason odds. The Twins parted ways with Baldelli after 2025, when the Twins again finished fourth in the Central. Baldelli’s playing career was unfortunately cut short because he battles mitochondrial channelopathy, a rare genetic condition that affects how mitochondria in your cells produce energy, which can cause a host of issues, from fatigue to diabetes to persistent muscle weakness or pain. The Mariners will now turn their attentions elsewhere as they continue to narrow their pool of candidates, as reportedly they were hoping to make a hire before the end of the month. They’ll have plenty of competition in attracting said candidates even in just the AL West, with both the Astros and the Angels looking for new managers. The Astros made a hiring move today, hiring Conner Watson away from the Cleveland Guardians, to be hitting director. Watson served as the Guardians’ assistant director of hitting development for the past two years; previously he was with Driveline in their Arizona location, serving as the Hitting Lead for four years after coming out of the small-college coaching corps.

item.title: Scout team success earned Brennan Ward a key touchdown in Kentucky’s win vs. Vanderbilt
item.description: If you forgot Brennan Ward is on the Kentucky Football roster, you probably aren’t alone. The fourth-string quarterback had not seen any live game action until the Vanderbilt matchup. 2nd-string QB Callum Wither threw an incomplete pass against South Alabama and appeared against Youngstown State, while Matt Ponatoski took a few snaps vs. South Alabama, but no other quarterback had seen the field. That cameo against Vandy didn’t surprise his head coach or his fellow teammates. Ward runs the Kentucky scout team whenever the defense faces a running quarterback. That means he spent weeks simulating mobile threats like LaNorris Sellers, John Mateer, Sam Leavitt, Marcel Reed, and Keelon Russell. He performed so well in practice that the head coach told Joe Sloan to find a way to get Ward in the game. “This week, I made it mandatory. I said, get him something that he can run the ball,” said Stein. “I love what Joe came up with. It was great, especially with two quarterbacks on the field. It was definitely an impressive run and play.” Safety Ty Bryant noted how “proud” he was when Ward scored. Bryant explained that coaches often claim they evaluate scout team performance, and this moment proved the Kentucky staff actually means it. This approach shows the coaching staff evaluates every player every time they step on the field. That breeds real competition every time any player steps on the field. They believe they will get a chance in a live game if they perform well in practice. Of course, that is how it should be. But if you have played competitive sports, you know that some guys are there just to be bodies and to simulate things. The mentality of everything matters permeates the entire Kentucky roster. Will Stein previously stated he refuses to waste any practice time, and players noted how different the spring program was. There were no breaks, and Stein said he wanted everything to flow from one thing to another. He even skipped releasing a spring depth chart because he prefers rotating players to see how they perform, and if they play well, they play more in the games. This strategy keeps the roster invested, and that means practices are intense. Those practices lead to moments like Saturday night, when Ward heard his number called and answered with a touchdown. HOW ABOUT @brennenward4 📺 – SEC Network pic.twitter.com/fK5CfHaWOR — Kentucky Football (@UKFootball) October 25, 2026 With mobile quarterbacks looming on the schedule against Florida, Missouri, and Louisville, fans might see even more of Ward on the field before the season ends.

item.title: Which NFL teams are still undefeated? Updated standings for Week 7 after Chiefs, 49ers fall for first time
item.description: Which NFL teams are still undefeated? Updated standings for Week 7 after Chiefs, 49ers fall for first time originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 1972 Dolphins shouldn't celebrate yet, but the ranks of the undefeated were thinned again in Week 7. The 49ers suffered a 29-20 road loss to the Falcons , dropping from 6-0 to 6-1 after an impressive start to the season. San Francisco had managed to power through a plethora of injuries, especially on offense, but Christian McCaffrey being forced to miss a chunk of the Week 7 matchup vs. Atlanta proved fatal. The Chiefs , who were the NFL's last remaining unbeaten team in 2024, joined the 49ers as previously-undefeated squads to suffer their first loss this week as well. Kansas City had zero answers for the defending champion Seattle Seahawks , falling 20-3 in the Pacific Northwest in what was one of the worst offensive showings in the Patrick Mahomes era. While it may only be a matter of time until the NFL's only wire-to-wire undefeated team knows its place in history is safe once again, the buzz will continue into November. Here's a look at which teams are still undefeated. MORE: Ranking the worst losses in upset-filled Week 7 Which NFL teams are still undefeated? Vikings (6-0) Do you believe in the Vikings yet? Some don't because Minnesota's offense has been inconsistent, but the defense is playing like the best in the NFL. The Vikings are allowing an average of just 10.4 points per game since allowing 22 in their season opener, and they shut out the Colts in the second half on Sunday to keep their perfect record intact. Fittingly, Minnesota ended the game by intercepting Daniel Jones. The Vikings have wins over the Packers , Bears, Buccaneers , Dolphins, Saints and Colts, but their schedule is also about to get much more difficult. Minnesota goes to Detroit, Green Bay and San Francisco in the next four weeks, with a matchup against the Bills also in that stretch. item.title: Maple Leafs HC Jim Hiller Provides Update on Injured Veterans
item.description: Chris Tanev Maple Leafs Jim Hiller John Tavares Getty Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller provided an update on two of the team’s injured players, veterans Chris Tanev and John Tavares. Tanev has been on the IR since October 12, retroactive to October 10, with an upper-body injury, while Tavares has been on the IR since October 17 with a lower-body injury. The Maple Leafs are rolling now with four straight wins, but there is no doubt both players returning would strengthen Toronto’s lineup. So, when are they coming back? Jim Hiller Gives Update on Chris Tanev & John Tavares Speaking to reporters at Maple Leafs practice on Sunday, Hiller was asked what the latest injury update on Tanev and Tavares is, and this is what the head coach said. “It looks like Chris is closer than John is, with him out on the ice (skating). That’s always a good sign when you start seeing the players get on the ice; he’s doing some one-on-ones, not heavy contact, but those are important steps, so we’re happy to have him doing that,” Hiller said. Maple Leafs Rolling The Maple Leafs are one of the hottest teams in the league right now as Toronto has won four straight games, including a blowout 7-2 win over the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday night that showed this Toronto team is for real this season. Captain Auston Matthews is having a bounce-back year, while winger William Nylander just scored his 300th career goal . Goalies Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz have also been fantastic this season in net for Toronto, as both goalies have stopped some key shots by the Maple Leafs’ opponents to keep them in the game. Obviously, Toronto had a really tough year last season, missing the playoffs for the first time in a decade, which led to the ouster of former GM Brad Treliving and former head coach Craig Berube. But with Hiller as the team’s new head coach and with new GM John Chayka pulling the strings from the front office, this Maple Leafs team looks legit this year, and they’ll look even better once Tanev and Tavares both get back into the team’s lineup. item.title: Knicks match troubling trend last seen in 2011 after loss to Magic
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Knicks match troubling trend last seen in 2011 after loss to Magic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks have already hit unsettling NBA history early in 2026 . But Sunday’s 111-102 loss to the Orlando Magic matched a troubling trend not seen since 2011. New York has now fallen to 0-3, leading to this mark mentioned by ClutchPoints NBA insider Brett Siegel. “The Knicks are the first defending champions since the Mavericks in 2011 to lose each of their first three games of the new season,” Siegel posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Yes, the season is a long one and it’s only three games. But Siegel brought up one more historical nugget involving the winless champs. “Dallas went on to lose in the first round of the playoffs that year as the defending champions,” Siegel adds. So the Knicks have new concerning marks attached to them. And even their ring ceremony came with controversy. Owner James Dolan reportedly used a scam email to employees about getting their rings. But claimed it was to ease cybersecurity concerns. Still, Dolan drew lots of heat for the tactic. The Knicks immediately owned the mistake there. But that’s not the only ring controversy. Members of the Knicks coaching staff outside of coach Mike Brown never received their rings on opening night. So those coaches are still awaiting for their bling. Jalen Brunson led NYK with 28 points in 32 minutes on the floor against the Magic. Karl Anthony-Towns added 22 points along with OG Anunoby. Josh Hart rose as the last member of the Knicks to score past the double digit mark with 13 points in the loss. item.title: LAFC clinch Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs spot
item.description: LAFC clinch Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs spot By MLSsoccer staff LAFC have qualified for the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs, clinching their spot following a 2-2 draw vs. arch-rivals LA Galaxy on Sunday. With two regular-season matches left, the Black & Gold are sixth in the Western Conference table (47 points; 12W-9L-11D). After parting ways with head coach Marc Dos Santos in late September, LAFC are led by interim head coach Xavi Tamarit. LAFC won MLS Cup presented by Audi in 2022, beating the Philadelphia Union on penalty kicks. They also made the final in 2023 before falling to the Columbus Crew . Star players Star forwards Son Heung-Min and Denis Bouanga form a dynamic duo for LAFC, combining for 25g/24a. Bouanga recently became the second player in MLS history to score at least 80 goals over four seasons. Meanwhile, Son brings extensive Premier League and South Korea international experience into the postseason. French goalkeeper Hugo Lloris has posted 12 clean sheets this season, which is tied for third-best in the league. The 2018 FIFA World Cup champion backstops a defense led by Ryan Porteous and Aaron Long . This summer, midfielder Mathieu Choinière and winger Jacob Shaffelburg represented Canada at the 2026 World Cup. WATCH: El Tráfico delivers! LAFC, LA Galaxy battle to wild draw Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs MLS Cup presented by Audi will be played Dec. 18, while the playoffs begin Nov. 18 with Wild Card matches. Seeds 1-7 in each conference qualify for the Round One Best-of-3 Series. Seeds 8-9 in each conference qualify for the Wild Card matches. item.description: 🎥 Drama galore as LAFC and Galaxy finish level There were major fireworks in Los Angeles as the city's two bitter rivals, LAFC and LA Galaxy finished level in a crucial MLS showdown. The Galaxy had a two-goal lead in the second half and looked well on their way towards a famous victory in the home of their rivals, but Denis Bouanga, Son Heung-min and co. came racing back with two goals of their own. The major drama came with the final kick of the game when it appeared LAFC had snatched a late winner from a goalmouth scramble, but amid the delirious celebrations inside of BMO Stadium, the referee waved the goal off for a narrow offside in the buildup to the goal. This rivalry never disappoints and it certainly didn't tonight, yet both teams will feel frustrated to have not taken all three points.

Alex Caruso and Kenrich Williams were two veterans OKC relied on to spark some energy as it forced turnovers every other possession. Eventually, the Thunder had a 77-76 lead after the third quarter. Gilgeous-Alexander turned into a one-man scoring machine. Ajay Mitchell rediscovered his touch around the rim. Things were going well as it looked like OKC would get by with a close — but ugly — win over a rebuilding LA squad. And then Williams' devastating injury happened. As Williams went up for a driving dunk, Kris Dunn crashed into him mid-air. His left leg was then trapped underneath him. It bent in the wrong direction. The Thunder medical staff quickly wrapped it in towels. Gilgeous-Alexander and the rest of OKC knelt and were in tears. As he was slowly put on a stretcher, the quiet OKC crowd chanted his nickname and barked in support. The Thunder eventually closed things out. Dunn was handed a flagrant foul for what he did to Williams. They scored 31 points to squeak by. Darius Garland tried to get them back into it to no avail. Chet Holmgren had 10 points and four rebounds. Hartenstein finished with a 12-point, 12-rebound double-double. Mitchell dropped 18 points and six rebounds. Caruso had 12 points, seven rebounds and six assists. Meanwhile, the Clippers shot 46% from the field and went 15-of-38 (39.5%) from 3. They shot 12-of-15 on free throws. They had 30 assists on 37 baskets. Seven Clippers players scored double-digit points. Garland had 16 points and 11 assists. Dunn finished with 15 points and six assists. Derrick Jones Jr. finished with 11 points and six rebounds. Brook Lopez scored 15 points off of the bench. Kobe Sanders had 12 points and four rebounds. Jackson had 10 points and six rebounds. He contorted his body to get around Dunn's contest a few times for flashy layups. While the rest of the Thunder took care of business on defense, he put their head above water on offense as the sole creator. Eventually, Gilgeous-Alexander slammed shut the door. He shot Williams' free throws after Dunn's flagrant foul. Obviously, though, he was on autopilot. And so was the rest of the Thunder and OKC crowd. item.title: Luke Bryan's son commits to Georgia, fulfilling childhood dream
item.description: Luke Bryan's son commits to Georgia, fulfilling childhood dream originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Bo Bryan will have his opportunity to suit up for the Georgia Bulldogs . The son of country music star Luke Bryan is preparing to hit the ground running with the program he has been rooting for since his childhood. The three-star quarterback from Battle Ground Academy in Franklin, Tennessee, committed to Georgia on Sunday, becoming the program's second quarterback pledge in the 2027 recruiting class. He joins four-star prospect Colton Nussmeier. Bryan's commitment came just five days after Georgia offensive coordinator Mike Bobo extended his first Power Four scholarship offer. Bryan accepted during the phone call. "As soon as I got the call, I knew," Bryan told On3 . "I knew that I was ready to do it. I literally committed on the phone with Coach Bobo. It was literally a dream come true." At 6-foot-1 and 200 pounds, Bryan is not a highly ranked prospect by national recruiting standards. The 247Sports Composite ranks him No. 2,052 nationally and No. 141 among quarterbacks. Before Georgia's offer, his scholarship opportunities came from Football Championship Subdivision programs. However, Bryan has delivered strong numbers in his first season as Battle Ground Academy's full-time starter. He completed 114 of 155 passes for 2,006 yards, 30 touchdowns and three interceptions while leading his team to a 7-1 record. The Bryan family has a connection to UGA. Luke Bryan has frequently expressed his loyalty to the program. Bo grew up attending games and idolizing former Georgia stars. Bryan plans to sign with Georgia in December and enroll in January, turning a childhood dream into a reality. item.title: The 49ers’ playoff picture is still rosy
item.description: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers suffered their first loss of the season. Here’s how the playoff picture and divisional standings shake out. NFC West standings before Week 8 1. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 2. Seattle Seahawks (4-3) 3. Los Angeles Rams (3-4) 4. Arizona Cardinals (2-5) We’ll have a more thorough update about the division first thing Monday morning, but here’s a look at the standings. The 49ers are 3-0 in the division. Seattle is 1-1. The Rams are 0-2 — something that could come back to bite them down the line. NFC playoff standings after Week 7 1. Minnesota Vikings (6-0) 2. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 3. New York Giants (4-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-3) 5. Chicago Bears (5-2) 6. Detroit Lions (4-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (4-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (4-3) 9. Atlanta Falcons (3-4, 3-2 NFC) 10. Los Angeles Rams (3-4, 2-2 NFC) 11. Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) – Monday Night Football 12. Dallas Cowboys (2-4) – Monday Night Football 13. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5, 1-0 NFCS) 14. New Orleans Saints (2-5, 0-1 NFCS, 1-3 NFC) 15. Arizona Cardinals (2-5, 1-4 NFC) 16. Washington Commanders (1-4-1) The 49ers have a date with the Vikings in a few weeks. So they’ll have an opportunity to regain the No. 1 seed. The Niners would also have the head-to-head advantage over Minnesota if it came down to a tiebreaker at season’s end. A quick look at the Vikings’ schedule makes you think they’ll be lucky to make the playoffs, let alone earn a bye. Yes, they’re undefeated, but the Vikings face the Lions twice, Bills, Packers, Niners, Falcons, Panthers, Patriots, and Bears to end the season. Those are all coin-flip games. J.J. McCarthy leading the Giants to a division win would sum up the NFL: You never know what’s going to happen. McCarthy wasn’t great on a down-to-down basis, but he made a few big-time plays when New York needed him to. There’s still a lot of football to play. Carolina leads the NFC South, but they took it to the chin in Week 7. That division is far from solved. Tampa Bay’s defense looks for real. I wouldn’t count them out. Green Bay has the talent, but they are not a buttoned-up team. The Seahawks had over 400 yards against the Chiefs, but are you scared of that offense? Their defense is scary, but Sam Darnold is inevitable. The Falcons are inconsistent, but they’ve proven they can beat anyone on any given Sunday. They’re talented, but probably a year away. The longer the Rams stick around, the more chances they get to get healthy and make a playoff run.

item.title: Packers’ Josh Jacobs apologizes to team after crucial blunder in loss to Lions
item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Packers’ Josh Jacobs apologizes to team after crucial blunder in loss to Lions appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Josh Jacobs held himself accountable after making a crucial mistake in the Green Bay Packers’ 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon. The drop came on 3rd-and-5. Had he caught the pass, Jacobs would have scored a 17-yard touchdown and put the Packers up 24-17. Instead, the Packers brought out rookie kicker Trey Smack for a 35-yard field goal, which was partially blocked and ended up no good. Jacobs reflected on his error after the game, per reporter Ryan Wood. Accountability was on the running back’s mind as he apologized to his team for not getting the job done in that moment. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “After the game, Josh Jacobs said he apologized to his team for dropping Jordan Love’s TD pass on third-and-5 with 3:30 left. Big turn in the loss,” Wood wrote. “I apologized to the guys,” Jacobs said. “At the end of the game, I called that play, where I dropped that touchdown in the end zone. For my standard, I like myself 10/10. That’s a play I gotta make. If you want to blame anybody, blame me.” After the game, Josh Jacobs said he apologized to his team for dropping Jordan Love’s TD pass on third-and-5 with 3:30 left. Big turn in the loss. “That’s a play I’ve got to make. So I said, ‘If you want to blame anybody, put it on me.’” pic.twitter.com/6DqSxyw5bb — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) October 26, 2026 How Josh Jacobs, Packers played against Lions Josh Jacobs is glad to be back in action. However, he will have to minimize the risk of mistakes moving forward as he gets himself back in form to the Packers’ benefit. Both teams traded blows throughout the course of the game, only seeing Detroit lead 10-7 at halftime. They were even at 17 apiece going into the fourth quarter, but Lions kicker Jake Bates sealed the deal with a game-winning field goal from 22 yards to send Green Bay packing. Jordan Love delivered decent performance as he kept his receivers active. He completed 27 out of 45 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns and an interception. Jacobs made his season debut with 11 carries for 36 yards while catching five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown. Christian Watson led receivers with five catches for 57 yards, while Tucker Kraft caught four passes for 48 yards and a touchdown. The Packers will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being at home. They host the Carolina Panthers in Week 8 as kickoff commences on Oct. 29 at 8:15 p.m. ET. item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
